records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:616 — Repeatedly formatting the entire accumulated ID string makes SQLite query construction quadratic in batch size, causing excessive allocation and copying for large batches.
records.rationale: The finding points to line 616 in xorm_store.go where the code builds the ID string for SQLite queries. Looking at the diff, lines 595-599 show: `values := fmt.Sprint(ids[0])` followed by a loop `for _, v := range ids[1:] { values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) }`. This is indeed quadratic string concatenation - each iteration creates a new string by copying the entire previous string plus the new value. For large batches (the test shows batches up to 32767), this causes O(n²) allocations and copying. This is a real performance defect in the newly introduced code.
